later.subject: Keep the fleet invariant in the tick and remove the session host's own wake and stall: every tick checks each non-stopped box worker on its host that has no open gate and completed its last turn within 48 hours, and requires it to be running, finished with a final report or a question, or parked on a wait whose deadline has not passed and whose job lease has not lapsed, judged on the store host's clock (the exchange now returns the store's time and the addressees' fleet_waits rows); otherwise it hands in a wake with the reason ("your job X's lease lapsed with no exit", "wait X passed its deadline", or "parked with no registered wait" after two ticks of grace for a JOB-START still in a spool), at most four wakes a tick, and after three wakes of one worker tells its parent instead. A turn is known by its session stream's length, so a stream rebuild never makes an old stop look new. Lapse checks are skipped only for a machine whose spool could not be taken that tick; a row the store refuses is now set aside under spool/rejected/ on its machine (north fleet spool set-aside) with a notice, so it no longer marks the machine failed on every tick. Lapsed and overdue waits are settled in the store (north fleet row settle), and a settlement the ledger host did not confirm is retried on the next tick. The tick also runs the farm, branch, capture, job and pid probes that north fleet waits ran from dispatch and laptop-runner. The session host no longer wakes a worker on its waiting text, stalls it, or messages a detached run's end: it registers each live detached run as a pid wait, keeps holding the session unparked while the run lives, and leaves the run's end to the tick's probe, so nothing wakes twice; its silent notice still covers an interrupted turn. The 48-hour window, longer than the longest default wait deadline, keeps the 328 old parked box workers on the laptop from being revived at deploy (north#429 box 3b)

later.subject: Cloud sessions push their own claude/land-* branches, so couriers stop landing on Nexus (north#216)
later.body:
About a dozen courier sessions on Nexus applied cloud handbacks, reran checks and landed them, holding its three cores at a load of 55-81 and stalling landings for over an hour; Tom asked to fix why Nexus lands at all rather than move couriers (2026-10-26). Cloud sessions had no GitHub write access, and the Claude GitHub App installed that day lets a session launched from a checkout of its repository push.

later.subject: Admit gex45 fleet rows only as its own and drain a remote ledger only from a configured job source
later.body:
D2 boxes B4 and B5 of the gex45 least-privilege plan (2026-11-04), with the
fixes from the B5 review of the same day.

B4: north laptop-runner polls the threads ledger of a remote host only when
its [hosts.NAME] sets job_source = true, so a job queued in gex45's own
ledger never runs as tom on the laptop or Nexus.

B5: fleet::peer_row admits a row from a peer only when from names the peer,
its sender is a session the ledger lists on the peer, and every kind but
MESSAGE (CONTROL, GATE, GATE-ANSWER, JOB-START, JOB-BEAT, JOB-EXIT) is
addressed to a session on the peer. The ledger's one record per name decides;
a name another host holds is never the peer's, and the sessions an exchange
carries never vouch for its own rows. Admitted rows carry origin.

north fleet row put|exchange|register|wait|settle --peer HOST apply it: the
put and wait forwards keep --peer for the ledger host, register and take-over
refuse a name another host holds, wait and settle reach only the peer's
sessions, and an exchange drops addressees and gates that are not the peer's
and returns other hosts' sessions as name, host and status only, with no rows,
gates or waits of theirs. The dispatcher forcing --peer is left to B8.

take_far applies it to every pulled far spool, reading the ledger's cached
record before a local one. An unregistered row stays for the next tick for at
most the launch grace, then is set aside, except a MESSAGE whose sender is a
retired session archived here as placed on that peer, which is delivered.

The adversarial review of the same day found gex45 paths still open.
Tom restated on 2026-11-04 that gex45 has no authority over the laptop, so
every check here fails closed:

- the laptop's tick admits gex45's registry reply through admit_exchange
  under the configured far host name before it reaches the ledger, so a reply
  naming the laptop or its lead can neither rewrite the lead nor have the
  laptop ship the lead's rows to gex45;
- laptop runners drain a remote ledger only when its host sets
  job_source = true, so a host with no setting, gex45 today, is skipped;
- the fleet row verbs refuse to run unchecked when entered through a forced
  ssh command, or for a NORTH_REMOTE_PEER that --peer does not name;
- an unregistered row is held only while its sent_at is within the launch
  grace of the tick in either direction, so a future sent_at is not held
  forever;
- a peer registers only names the ledger already lists as its own or new
  names starting with PEER-, a host's own tick outranks the far hosts it
  pulls when it publishes a name one of them took first, a peer's exchange
  can never outrank anyone, a peer's registration is stamped with the
  ledger's clock, and its addressees read nothing sent before that stamp;
- a peer's MESSAGE to a session not on the peer is never urgent.

Also gives two integration-test rows the origin field B5 added.

later.subject: Keep the fleet invariant in the tick and remove the session host's own wake and stall: every tick checks each non-stopped box worker on its host that has no open gate and completed its last turn within 48 hours, and requires it to be running, finished with a final report or a question, or parked on a wait whose deadline has not passed and whose job lease has not lapsed, judged on the store host's clock (the exchange now returns the store's time and the addressees' fleet_waits rows); otherwise it hands in a wake with the reason ("your job X's lease lapsed with no exit", "wait X passed its deadline", or "parked with no registered wait" after two ticks of grace for a JOB-START still in a spool), at most four wakes a tick, and after three wakes of one worker tells its parent instead. A turn is known by its session stream's length, so a stream rebuild never makes an old stop look new. Lapse checks are skipped only for a machine whose spool could not be taken that tick; a row the store refuses is now set aside under spool/rejected/ on its machine (north fleet spool set-aside) with a notice, so it no longer marks the machine failed on every tick. Lapsed and overdue waits are settled in the store (north fleet row settle), and a settlement the ledger host did not confirm is retried on the next tick. The tick also runs the farm, branch, capture, job and pid probes that north fleet waits ran from dispatch and laptop-runner. The session host no longer wakes a worker on its waiting text, stalls it, or messages a detached run's end: it registers each live detached run as a pid wait, keeps holding the session unparked while the run lives, and leaves the run's end to the tick's probe, so nothing wakes twice; its silent notice still covers an interrupted turn. The 48-hour window, longer than the longest default wait deadline, keeps the 328 old parked box workers on the laptop from being revived at deploy (north#429 box 3b)

later.subject: Keep the fleet invariant in the tick and remove the session host's own wake and stall: every tick checks each non-stopped box worker on its host that has no open gate and completed its last turn within 48 hours, and requires it to be running, finished with a final report or a question, or parked on a wait whose deadline has not passed and whose job lease has not lapsed, judged on the store host's clock (the exchange now returns the store's time and the addressees' fleet_waits rows); otherwise it hands in a wake with the reason ("your job X's lease lapsed with no exit", "wait X passed its deadline", or "parked with no registered wait" after two ticks of grace for a JOB-START still in a spool), at most four wakes a tick, and after three wakes of one worker tells its parent instead. A turn is known by its session stream's length, so a stream rebuild never makes an old stop look new. Lapse checks are skipped only for a machine whose spool could not be taken that tick; a row the store refuses is now set aside under spool/rejected/ on its machine (north fleet spool set-aside) with a notice, so it no longer marks the machine failed on every tick. Lapsed and overdue waits are settled in the store (north fleet row settle), and a settlement the ledger host did not confirm is retried on the next tick. The tick also runs the farm, branch, capture, job and pid probes that north fleet waits ran from dispatch and laptop-runner. The session host no longer wakes a worker on its waiting text, stalls it, or messages a detached run's end: it registers each live detached run as a pid wait, keeps holding the session unparked while the run lives, and leaves the run's end to the tick's probe, so nothing wakes twice; its silent notice still covers an interrupted turn. The 48-hour window, longer than the longest default wait deadline, keeps the 328 old parked box workers on the laptop from being revived at deploy (north#429 box 3b)

landings.subject: Add north watch --once with work probes that name stalled in-progress work in every project
landings.body:
Tom asked on 2026-11-04 to learn of any hiccup in any project's work within a minute, after builds sat 20 min in the laptop queue unseen, workers parked on finished background runs looked idle, runtime-follow abandoned 17 builds in 3 hours and a red main went 35 min unnoticed. Each probe is fn(&WatchContext) -> Vec<Alert> in the contract agreed with the land-watch sink (stable key, severity, repo, owner, one-line summary, since), and one pass gathers the snapshot in parallel and runs them all:

- capacity: a ticket queued past max(5 min, its predicted wait p90) on any host read over ssh, or the laptop's CPU PSI some avg10 above its profile's admission high mark for 2 min while work queues
- workers: a fleet session working past twice its brief ETA, or silent 10 min with no registered wait; a running cloud session silent 10 min (an Info alert when north cloud list itself fails); a Claude Code subagent whose transcript last moved over 10 min ago while a background shell output it started was written after that and is no longer held open, read from file metadata only
- waits: a north fleet wait run past its expected duration (farm 45 min, capture 30 min, others 60 min)
- runtime-follow: more than 3 abandoned builds in 30 min, read from a new runtime-abandoned journal north runtime now appends to when origin/main supersedes a build, or the live runtime more than 15 min behind a Rust change on origin/main
- hosts: an orchestration.toml host unreachable over ssh (5 s connect timeout) for 2 min, as a page
- waste: work waiting over 60 s while its host's measured live CPU is under 70% of its cores and over 25% of memory is free (thresholds in harness/defaults.toml), one page per visible cause: game reserve on with no game seen for 10 min, every offload slot of a pool held, CPU commit accounting at its limit far above live use, a lease holding CPUs at zero live cores for over an hour, else unexplained; these carry a 15 min repeat, added to the contract as Alert.repeat_secs at the coordinator's request

Durations and first-seen times that need history across passes live in ~/.local/state/north/watch/probe-since.json. Tests: cargo test -p north-core --lib ops::watch 23 of 23 (a raising and a quiet fixture per probe, one pass running every probe, the source parsers), ops::runtime 9 of 9, clippy -p north-core -p north --all-targets clean

landings.subject: Route tiers on sound statistics and let north tune's route cells drive dispatch (north#242, north#112)
landings.body:
worker-ledger --recommend picked claude:opus-high for tooling/exact/cross-module on 2 successes of 6 runs, because it
priced by allocated plan dollars, compared raw rates and let a 5-run tier win on cost. It now:
- prices each run in API-equivalent dollars from ledger/prices.json (PriceTable::run_usd, the one definition the
  closed-box report, dispatch and tune now share; Haiku 5.5's $0.10/$0.50 checked against the cited page);
- shrinks each tier's success toward the category's pooled rate with a Beta prior worth ARM_RUNS (15) runs and uses
  that estimate for the pass test, the incumbent margin and $ per expected success;
- needs 15 priced runs (usd_min = ARM_RUNS) before a tier can win on cost;
- never picks the escalation-only tiers, Opus high and xhigh;
- falls back to the workers skill's default for the category, with the reason printed, when nothing qualifies;
- prints the chosen tier's shrunk success with its n and every tier's shrunk rate.

Dispatch and fleet launch follow the `route CATEGORY` cell north tune writes to ~/.local/state/north/tune/cells.json
while the file is under 36 h old, and settle the same Evidence::settled rule live otherwise, so the daily tick changes
a default with no human edit.

Fixtures whose expected tier changed: the recommend tests grew from 5 to 15 runs per tier so the cost and rank rules
they pin still have enough priced runs; the incumbent fixture moved to 30 runs a tier so the shrunk gap between
tiers still straddles the 15-point margin; thin and knob-override tests now expect "< 15" and the skill default where
they expected no tier; the verb golden prints the shrunk lines and "$ n/a" since its rows carry no tokens; the
defaults_measure fixture schema gained the token columns recommend reads.

later.subject: Hold an admitted native lease's Warcraft client slots until its clients start, so a later start can't take them and a pair's own client launches draw on its hold (Fixes #358)
later.body:
Admission compared running Warcraft clients plus the request against the
cap, so a pair session admitted with --new-clients 2 reserved nothing
until its clients launched. On the GPU host on 2026-10-29 a pool started 30 s
later took the slots and pair 0's client waited 480 s on
DEFER_GPU_CLIENTS (capture batch bmvtzvtag).

A native lease now records newClients and the lease it was started
inside. Until client_reserve_seconds (900) pass, each holds its
newClients less the clients it has started: the most seen running in
its scope (kept as clientsSeen) or the clients of the native leases
started inside it (added to clientsStarted when each is created), so the
hold doesn't return when its clients exit, even ones that ended before
any admission saw them run. Admission counts the held slots against the cap. A request from
inside a holding lease, as a pair session's own client launch is, draws
its clients from that hold; waiters queued ahead are still judged
against the whole hold, so one the hold keeps out doesn't stall the
pair's own launch. The scope regex nested batch runs used moves to
machine::enclosing_lease, which AGENT_CAPACITY_SELF_CGROUP overrides for
tests as the gate already does.

landings.body:
north fleet spool take lists each spool file as {id, row} without decoding it, and the pulling side decodes row by row: a row this build cannot read (an old ANSWER kind or a newer kind) is set aside on its machine through spool set-aside with a notice and never turns the machine into pull_failed, so every other row is still delivered and the lapse check stays on. spool drop and set-aside read their ids from stdin, so 5,000 ids no longer ride one argv string. A row file removed between listing and reading is skipped. OverSsh::through(path) lets the ssh client test run the real over_ssh quoting against a fake ssh binary. fleet list --json --all marks a remote row stale after 5 minutes without a publish, and only this host's live sessions hide a remote row of the same name, so an archived local session no longer does. Follows the post-landing review of boxes 2a and 4b.

The review gate covers none of these paths; a fresh Opus reviewer read the diff anyway. It found two integration tests (fleet_relay, fleet_launch) still reading the old take output, fixed here, and noted that a valid row of a newer kind is set aside by an older puller, which the box specifies.

later.subject: Make a fleet launch's exit status mean its session is running: stop a session that fails its first turn, say whose claim a launch took over, and hold a launch on a saturated host until admitted (north#346)
later.body:
A launch whose session exits or stalls before its first turn now stops it, so the failed
session releases its claim instead of staying parked on it. A claim an exited session left,
or one past its ETA, moves to the new session without --force-dup, and the launch prints the
ledger's line naming the earlier owner; a live or parked holder still refuses. Placement now
tells a saturated host (admission queue, disk, load) from a final refusal: with --wait, the
default when a lead launches, the launch prints the reason every minute and starts once
admitted, giving up after two hours; --no-wait refuses at once.

Fixes #346

later.subject: Port worker-ledger to `north worker-ledger` and record Claude, Codex and agy runs, summaries and recommendations in Rust (north#88)
later.body:
`north worker-ledger [--session ID] [--since DATE] [--backfill]` records
finished workers through `north threads run-ids|ingest` from the Claude
runs reader, a new Codex rollout reader (providers/codex/runs) and a new
agy reader (providers/agy) that share the ledger row helpers in
providers/ledger_rows, then recalibrates in Rust: `threads calibrate
--write` on the ledger host when the newest calibration row is over
calibrate_after_min old, and `defaults-measure --priors` recorded as prior
rows once a week from Monday 00:00Z where Codex rollouts exist.
`--summary` and `--recommend [--planner]` run `north threads summary` and
`recommend`. For the context and fleet fixtures the runs, usage samples
and printed summary and recommendations match the shell tool's.

bin/worker-ledger, its test, harness/lib/recalibrate.py and the Python
usage, hook, session-role and cost functions in ledger_context.py only
they used are deleted; the dispatch survey, threads, capacity-watchdog
and follows tests, the docs and the skills name `north worker-ledger`.
The nixos-config timer's ExecStart lands as its own change. The old shell
test is ported to tests/worker_ledger_record.rs plus a codex usage unit
test.

Review fixes: recalibration reads the ledger through the usage module (quick_check and one snapshot refresh) and bounds defaults-measure --priors at 600 s; a failing Codex or agy reader and an unreadable --since now fail the run (exit 1, exit 2); no current_exe fallback, one north() helper, the Python str() mapping and the widened visibility are gone; the plateau, same-window, wrong-account, early-reading, 40:1 split and byte-identical allocation checks are cargo tests in threads::runs, delivery_metrics is asserted in goal_eta.test.py, the telemetry-only replay asserts role and each recalibration run asserts exit 0.
